vitest 5 moved the benchmark options, and the type checker said so

PR playground for #3981: migrating src/hooks to vitest 5.0.0.

src/hooks is the only tree in the repo with a benchmark suite and the shared mock factories, so it was the only one that could not follow the vitest 5 bump the other four manifests already took. Five type errors, three distinct causes, and one the issue did not list: the bench config uses two options vitest 5 also removed.

The migration, by cause

RemovedReplacement
import { bench } from 'vitest'test-context fixture: test(name, async ({ bench }) => ...)
describe.sequentialplain describe; serial is the default
bare vi.fn() in 5 placesvi.fn<(...args: unknown[]) => void>()
benchmark.outputJson--reporter=json --outputFile=
benchmark.reporterstop-level test.reporters

The part worth remembering: options moved to the second argument

// v4, options third
bench('5KB - PAT embedded', () => { ... }, OPTS);

// v5: bench(name, BenchFnOptions, fn), and the sampling
// window is not BenchFnOptions at all. It is tinybench BenchOptions,
// which the API now takes at RUN time.
await bench('5KB - PAT embedded', () => { ... }).run(OPTS);

Passing { time, warmupTime, warmupIterations } in the registration slot fails with TS2559 "no properties in common". That is the good outcome. The bad one would have been a silent fall back to default sampling, leaving a benchmark that still prints numbers and no longer measures what its header says it measures.

TS2883 had a smaller fix than the issue proposed

The issue suggested annotating the three helpers' return types, awkward because the inferred type names Procedure from a hashed internal chunk path. But the trigger is narrower than the symptom: only a bare vi.fn() infers Mock<Procedure>. createFsMock and createPathMock never errored, because every one of their mocks has an implementation. Typing the five bare calls removes the unnameable reference without a single return-type annotation or cast.

Verification: a subset, not a promise

Same suite, same machine, main versus this branch.

vitestfiles failedtests failedpassed
main b37f3db924.1.117246615
this branch5.0.06236616

The remaining 6 failing files are a strict subset of main's 7, so the bump adds no failure and clears one. Those 6 are environmental on a dev machine: a missing plugins/ork/hooks/dist/*.map (release-owned, never committed, per #3578) and git commit inside test fixture repos. Typecheck went 5 errors to 0, and npm run bench exits 0 writing a 5.4KB artifact with real p50/p99/rme/samplesCount for all four benchmarks.

Reproduce it

cd src/hooks
npm install
npm run typecheck   # expect 0 errors
npm run bench       # expect exit 0 + bench-results.json
npm test
One deprecation observed and deliberately left alone: the bench config uses __dirname, which Vite warns will stop working under configLoader: 'native'. Unrelated to vitest 5, so it is not folded into a migration PR.
